questions.subject: MATH
questions.stem: During a review of the topic, in a structured way, solve the problem that follows: How many spanning trees does the complete graph K_7 have?

options.misconception: it uses the wrong exponent in Cayley's formula
it bases the power on n minus one
it counts all labelings rather than trees

questions.explanation: By Cayley's formula the number of spanning trees of K_7 is n to the power (7 minus 2), which equals 16807. Choice B is a distractor: it uses the wrong exponent in Cayley's formula. Choice C is a distractor: it bases the power on n minus one. Choice D is a distractor: it counts all labelings rather than trees.
questions.hint: Apply Cayley's formula n to the power n minus two.

questions.subject: MATH
questions.stem: For a take-home task, in a structured way, solve the problem that follows: From the complete graph K_7, how many edges are not used by a given spanning tree?

options.misconception: it ignores that the tree uses some edges

Choice C is a distractor: it reports the tree's own edges. Choice D is a distractor: it removes one edge too many.
questions.hint: Subtract the tree's n minus one edges from the total.

questions.stem: On a sample assessment, in a structured way, try this exercise: A complete binary tree has height 7. What is the maximum number of nodes it can contain?

options.misconception: it counts only the deepest level
it omits the final subtraction of one
it adds one instead of subtracting

questions.explanation: A complete binary tree of height 7 has all levels filled, giving 2 to the power (7+1) minus 1 nodes, namely 255. Choice B is a distractor: it counts only the deepest level. Choice C is a distractor: it omits the final subtraction of one. Choice D is a distractor: it adds one instead of subtracting.
questions.hint: Sum the geometric series of level sizes.

stimulus.body: In a discrete math review, consider the following question: A binary tree has 9 internal (non-leaf) nodes. How many external null leaves does it have?

questions.stem: In a guided example, in a structured way, try this exercise: A binary tree has 9 internal (non-leaf) nodes. How many external null leaves does it have?

options.misconception: it assumes equal numbers of internal and external nodes
it doubles the internal count
it subtracts instead of adding one

questions.explanation: In any binary tree the number of external leaves exceeds the number of internal nodes by one, so 9 internal nodes give 10 external leaves. Choice B is a distractor: it assumes equal numbers of internal and external nodes. Choice C is a distractor: it doubles the internal count. Choice D is a distractor: it subtracts instead of adding one.
questions.hint: External leaves are internal nodes plus one.
